rationale: F30 (2026-10-12), the svelte twin of vue/modern-html-svg-builtin-tags. The HTML/SVG builtin vocabulary in this analyzer and the vue lane's are held IDENTICAL by script/m14/verify-cross-language-consistency.ts, so when F30 added the SVG filter module and the rest of the element vocabulary to both, this lane inherited the fix — and inherited the obligation to prove it USES the set rather than merely declaring it. Set parity is a statement about two literals; it cannot see a filter call site that compares against the wrong thing, which is the failure mode this fixture exists to catch (the same distinction the lane's read map draws between a declared site list and the pass that reads it). The measurement lives in the vue twin: 441 fabricated instantiates edges over a 1,162-file draw — <filter> plus six primitives, 64 to 61 edges each, 377 of them pointing at no symbol anywhere in the corpus and 64 resolving against a symbol published by a DIFFERENT file, i.e. markup wearing a real component's name. `Child` is the over-suppression guard: the same template's real component must keep its instantiates row, so a fix that widened the reserve until nothing was a component would fail here rather than pass.

expectRelationships.comment: the over-suppression guard — a real component in the same template still publishes, so this fixture cannot be satisfied by silencing everything

forbidRelationships.comment: an SVG element the spec defines; it is markup whether or not the file is a .vue or a .svelte
measured on the vue corpus: 64 edges, the most common primitive
the wider vocabulary: never observed as a tag on this lane's corpus, and pinned anyway so a later narrowing of the builtin set fails here and not in a consumer
